stops.note: sailors measured speed with a wooden log on a knotted line, and recorded it in the 'log-book', giving 'log' as a daily record
Jorn Barger coined it in December 1997 for his site Robot Wisdom, a daily log of links from the World Wide Web
Peter Merholz jokingly split 'weblog' into 'we blog' on his site in 1999, and Blogger launched that August

current_meaning: a regularly updated website written in an informal or conversational style
